newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply down on pessimism.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply down on pessimism.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down on Wednesday on overwhelming pessimism about the short-term market trend in the wake of recent falls, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 19,800 yuan ($2,387) per tonne, losing 550 yuan. It opened at 20,100 and hit a high of 20,140 yuan per tonne.
August fell 360 to 19,940, September 480 to 19,820, October 580 to 19,800, December 500 to 19,850 and the January 1998 contract 450 to 19,870 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 64,400 tonnes from 78,970 tonnes.
Copper opened lower but mostly at intraday highs. Prices then fell steadily for the whole session before all contracts closed at their intraday lows, traders said.
Traders said recent falls had greatly weakened market sentiment with all contracts breaching the key support level of 20,000 yuan per tonne.
"Weak market sentiment was responsible for today's heavy losses and panic selling emerged after copper fell below 20,000 yuan," one trader said.
"But volume did not rise sharply indicating many investors also wished to bet on copper's rebound in the next few days," he said.
Physical prices fell to 19,900-20,000 yuan in the Shanghai area due to sharp falls on the futures market, traders said.
Traders said that depsite the market pessimism, further heavy losses were unlikely in the next few days.
"A bearish market mood will continue to prevail for a short period but sharp falls are unlikely with producers expected to sell less due to low prices," a second trader said.
Producer profits would be limited by the falls below 20,000 yuan, and this would make them reluctant to sell, traders said.
However, further slow falls were seen in the short term, they said.
Aluminium futures ended down. August fell 110 to 13,420, September 240 to 13,500, October 220 to 13,460, November 110 to 13,540 and December 190 to 13,460 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 3,020 tonnes from 3,660 tonnes.
